Guide\n\nA small, deterministic HTTP service for D&D 5e helper calculations. It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. Parameterized routes are placed before more general parents so they are not accidentally shadowed.\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- Any other HTTP method returns `405 Method Not Allowed` without reading the body.\n\n`POST` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`.
